title: A 20-Year-Old YouTuber Just Made A24's Biggest Film Ever. It Cost Less Than ₹85 Crore.
excerpt: Kane Parsons turned a creepy 4chan post into Backrooms — now A24's first $200 million film, made for under $10 million, and the most unlikely box office phenomenon of 2026.
body:
In 2019, an anonymous user posted a grainy photo on 4chan depicting an unsettling expanse of yellowed carpet, fluorescent lighting, and empty office corridors stretching into nowhere. The caption was simple. The image was creepy. And the internet did what the internet does — it built a mythology around it.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=0HjdiohVOik</youtube>

Seven years later, that mythology has a name, a director, and $212.6 million at the worldwide box office.

**Backrooms**, directed by 20-year-old **Kane Parsons** and released by **A24**, has officially become the studio's highest-grossing film of all time, overtaking **Timothée Chalamet**'s *Marty Supreme* ($191 million) in just 10 days. It's A24's first film to cross the $200 million mark. The production budget? Under $10 million.

Read that again. A horror film made for less than a Bollywood mid-budget production has outgrossed everything A24 has ever released — including *Everything Everywhere All at Once*, including *Marty Supreme*, including every prestige darling the studio has championed over the past decade.

> "I try to make what feels naturally compelling to me, what I have a natural intuition to try to make." — Kane Parsons

The film stars Oscar nominees **Chiwetel Ejiofor** and **Renate Reinsve**. Reinsve plays a therapist who enters the Backrooms — a liminal nightmare dimension beyond reality — to retrieve her patient (Ejiofor). If that sounds like a video game premise, that's partly the point. Parsons started making Backrooms content on YouTube at 16. His short films — lo-fi, eerie, and hypnotically watchable — went viral, racking up hundreds of millions of views. Hollywood came calling. A24 gave a teenager with no feature credits the keys to the car.

The gamble paid off spectacularly. The film opened to $81.5 million domestically, obliterating A24's previous best opening ($28.5 million for *Marty Supreme*). Parsons became the youngest director to debut at number one at the global box office, beating Josh Trank's record by seven years. By its second weekend, even with a steep 68% domestic drop — typical of fan-driven openings — the film had already rewritten every record A24 keeps.

Internationally, the numbers are staggering. Latin America leads all territories with $24.2 million, making it A24's highest-grossing title ever in the region. The UK sits at $11.6 million. Australia and New Zealand have already passed *Marty Supreme*. Spain posted a dominant $2 million second weekend. And 81% of the audience remains under 35 — this is overwhelmingly a film for the generation that grew up in the Backrooms' digital folklore.

What makes this story resonate beyond box office math is the pipeline it represents. Parsons joins **Curry Barker** (*Obsession*, $224 million on a $750,000 budget) and **Markiplier** (*Iron Lung*) as part of a new class of filmmakers who skipped film school, skipped the festival circuit, and built their audiences on YouTube instead. The "chronically online" generation isn't just watching movies anymore — they're making the biggest ones.

**For the diaspora**, *Backrooms* is already playing in Indian theatres (it released in 52 territories simultaneously) and should be widely available across US, UK, and Canadian multiplexes. If you've been on the fence: this is atmospheric, creepy, and wildly inventive horror that feels genuinely new. It's not a sequel, not a reboot, not IP extracted from a board game. It's a 4chan post that became a YouTube channel that became the most profitable A24 film in history.

That's either inspiring or terrifying, depending on how you feel about the internet's ability to manifest reality from nothing.

**A24** hasn't announced streaming plans yet, but given the studio's deal structures, expect a premium VOD window within 45-60 days of theatrical release. For now, this one earns the cinema screen.

*Backrooms is currently playing in theatres worldwide, including Indian, US, UK, and Canadian markets.*
